A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Direct Judgement Preference Optimization work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across 13 benchmarks, training ablations, bias and prompting analyses, and downstream model-training experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds critique-quality evaluation, contextual continual-finetuning experiments, and a teacher-quality ablation.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same CoT critique, standard judgement, and response deduction constructions, combined DPO+SFT objective, and underlying 8B/12B/70B models. The added studies investigate the existing recipe and its adaptation settings without introducing a new judge algorithm.

E1.justification: The original 13-benchmark suite remains, while v3 adds MetaCritique evaluation of critique factuality and completeness and ContextualJudgeBench evaluation of contextual pairwise judgements. The newly listed sources for the original training mixture are additional disclosure, not evidence that its coverage changed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 add Con-J-7B, Skywork-Critic-70B, Self-taught-evaluator-70B, and Themis-8B in relevant tasks. Prometheus-2-BGB and some FLAMe variants disappear from these comparisons, and Skywork-8B is removed from classification. Appendix E.9 additionally compares against DeepSeek-GRM and its inference-time scaling variants.

E3.justification: The existing benchmark metrics and response-order swapping procedure remain. New protocols include GPT-4-based MetaCritique scoring and contextual adaptation using 12,500 training samples, 2,000 test samples, an 80:20 CoT/standard-judgement mixture, three training epochs, and a five-value DPO beta sweep (Section 5.5; Appendix B.1).

E4.justification: v3 adds a strong-versus-weak negative-sample teacher ablation (Appendix E.8, Table 11) and a specialization/generalization sensitivity study through continual-finetuning beta values (Figure 6). Existing task ablations, prompting tests, bias analyses, and qualitative examples are retained, often in relocated sections.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The two response-order evaluations are retained. Newly disclosed sampling of 20 teacher responses concerns training-data generation, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The SFR scores in Tables 1–3 and the original ablation and downstream-refinement results remain unchanged. Substantial new results include MetaCritique F1 of 77.60 for SFR-Judge-70B, contextual accuracy of 55.6% versus 45.2% when finetuning from Llama-3.1-8B, and hard/easy-negative comparisons. These are additional experiments, not improvements to the retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The preference constructions and DPO+SFT mathematical objective are unchanged. Expanded notation and explanations of borrowed evaluation metrics introduce no new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: v3 replaces the headline claim of best performance on 10 of 13 benchmarks with best aggregate performance. It also adds central claims that the judges produce factual critiques and provide strong starting points for domain-specific continual finetuning, substantially expanding the foundational-judge contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning annotation freshness, English-only evaluation, complete versus partial responses, and inference cost. It also interprets harder negatives as mitigating positional bias, discusses specialization/generalization tradeoffs, and explains possible GPT-4-reference effects on MetaCritique recall.

D1.justification: v3 adds the training-source inventory in Table 5, teacher sampling settings, an EvalBiasBench prompt, and continual-finetuning construction and training details. A repository URL replaces v1's future-release promise. These substantially improve documentation, although v1's explicit 1024-token output limit is no longer specified.

R1.justification: v1 positions DPO as a departure from predecessors described as SFT-trained. v3 explicitly discusses DPO-based Themis, Self-taught Evaluator, and Con-J, distinguishing its multitask preference construction from their approaches. It also adds positioning relative to multitask learning and inference-time scaling.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Dataset descriptions and several main-text analyses move into reorganized appendices, while new analyses and limitations reshape the narrative. Model names are also shortened consistently.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, relocates and resizes existing displays, and adds training-source, critique-quality, teacher-ablation, and inference-scaling tables plus a continual-finetuning figure. Main-table highlighting changes from best overall/non-proprietary to best/second-best.

improvement.justification: Direct critique-quality evaluation addresses an important gap between correct judgements and trustworthy explanations, while controlled contextual finetuning strengthens evidence for transfer. More competitive baselines, revised novelty positioning, explicit training-source documentation, and substantive limitations substantially improve credibility and transparency. The original results remain stable, though statistical uncertainty is still unreported.
